issue.body:
### Vue version

3.2.36

### Link to minimal reproduction
[sfc.vuejs.org](https://sfc.vuejs.org/#)

### Steps to reproduce

* Optional: Make changes to the form. 
* Click the Reset input. 

### What is expected?

The form fields should be set to or stay at their initial values 
Select: "option two" 
Checkbox: checked 
Text: "text input value"

### What is actually happening?

The select is set to first option and the other fields are cleared.

### System Info

```shell
Reproducible in sfc.vuejs.org, code sandbox, Vue CLI, and custom build. 
Firefox, Chrome, Vivaldi.
Windows, Mac, Linux
```


### Any additional comments?

Inspect the code to see that the attributes selected, checked and value="text input value" have been removed in the Vue instance.

body:
A compiler optimization hoists these elements as one static HTML string, which removes the runtime type information that was present in the binding.
```js
const _hoisted_1 = /*#__PURE__*/_createStaticVNode("<option value=\"1\">One</option><option value=\"2\">Two</option><option value=\"3\">Three</option><option value=\"4\">Four</option><option value=\"5\">Five</option>", 5)
```

rename.from: Selects with more then 4 explictly typed options always return string values in v-model.
rename.to: Selects with more than 4 explictly typed options always return string values in v-model.

body:
as a workaround:
add a key to the option to avoid hoists.
```javascript
<select v-model="foo">
    <option :key="1" :value="1">One</option>
    ...
</select>
```

issue.title: fix(runtime-core): Select elements can preserve data types when stringified

repository.name: core
repository.description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.

issue.body:
close: #6568 
This pr is an enhancement to the stringification of `hoist static`. It takes effect when the data type bound to the element is `number`, `string`, `null`, or `boolean` in the stringification of the `option` tag.

1.It works in stringification of `option` tags. Because the stringification process is usually performed on static elements, but for form elements, the stringification of the `option` tag will affect the result of `v-model` on the `select` tag, ( Maybe there are other scenarios), so this `pr` only takes effect on the `option` tag

2.It is only valid for `number`, `string`, `null`, `boolean` data types bound to `option` tags, because for other data types, there is no guarantee that they can be safely and effectively converted to strings or serialized

issue.title: fix(compiler-dom): restrict createStaticVNode usage with option elements

repository.name: core
repository.description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.

issue.body:
Close #6568.

This fixes an edge case for code like this:

```html
<select v-model="foo">
  <option :value="1">...</option>
  <option :value="2">...</option>
  <option :value="3">...</option>
  <option :value="4">...</option>
  <option :value="5">...</option>
</select>
```

For 5 or more `<option>` elements, a static VNode is created. But this loses the type information on the `value`, so `v-model` treats it as a string.

- [Playground](https://play.vuejs.org/#)

There is already an existing PR that attempts to fix this problem, #7434. That PR attempts to add support for passing type information using `v-stringify-type='number'`. In my opinion, this edge case is not important enough to justify that extra complexity.

The fix I've attempted here will just bail out from using `createStaticVNode` if a non-string `value` is used with an `<option>`.

I'm not aware of any other elements that have this same problem. A checkbox or radio `<input>` can have a number for `value`, but the `v-model` will already avoid `createStaticVNode`. The problem with `<option>` occurs because the `v-model` is on the parent `<select>` instead.
